passage:
Aparna: hey. did i do something? you bit my head off when i asked about the trip
Usha: ugh. no. sorry
Usha: i hadn't eaten since morning. lab ran over and i skipped lunch
Aparna: ok but it kind of stung. i was only asking if you'd booked the tickets
Usha: i know. it wasn't about you. i was starving and everything felt like an attack
Aparna: fair. i've been there
Aparna: honestly i went home thinking you didn't want me on the trip anymore
Usha: noooo. i really do want you there
Usha: can we sort the tickets tomorrow after lunch? like actually after lunch
Aparna: deal. i'll bring samosas just in case
Usha: you're the best 🙏

qa.a: If Usha had booked the tickets.

qa.q: What was Aparna worried about after being snapped at?
qa.a: Aparna felt stung and worried that Usha no longer wanted Aparna on the trip.

qa.q: What do they agree to, and why is it a good plan?
qa.a: To sort the tickets tomorrow after lunch, so hunger is out of the way before they return to the real question.

qa.q: How did the moment look from Usha's side?
qa.a: Usha was starving after skipping lunch, so everything felt like an attack; the snap was about hunger, not Aparna.

grounding: Shows a friend snapped at by a hungry friend taking it personally, and both agreeing to eat first and revisit the real issue later.

passage: By late afternoon at the Hampi temple fair, old school friends Sangeeta and Naveen had been selling bangles since dawn without a break. When Sangeeta miscounted change for a customer, Naveen snapped, "Can't you do one simple thing right?" Her face went hot. She almost dropped the cash box and walked to the bus stand. Then she noticed his hands trembling as he tied a bundle, and remembered neither of them had eaten since the morning idlis. "Naveen. Food first. Then you can shout if you still want to." He opened his mouth, closed it and nodded. Over hot mirchi bajji from the next stall, his shoulders dropped. "Sorry. I was horrible." Later they sorted out the real problem: one of them would handle the cash box, the other the customers.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta and Naveen sell at the fair?
What was Sangeeta feeling right after Naveen snapped?
qa.a: She felt hurt and humiliated; her face went hot and she almost walked off to the bus stand.

qa.q: What choice kept the argument from growing, and why?
qa.a: Sangeeta suggested food first; once both had eaten, Naveen could apologise and they could sort out the cash box calmly.

qa.q: How might the afternoon have felt for Naveen before they ate?
qa.a: He was likely shaky and on edge from hunger, which made a small mistake feel like a big one.

grounding: Illustrates a friend snapped at after a long day without food, and both pausing to eat before sorting out the real issue.
